questions.question: How much process should this quick PR carry? Both errors are latent: an assistant record with usage but no `id` would make every later id-less call get skipped (undercount), and under `python -OO` `__doc__` is None so argparse setup crashes.

options.label: New BUG item, full protocol (Recommended)
options.description: Mint a BUG-xxx, register it done in BACKLOG-DONE, small trace, regression test seen failing first, then fix. Matches CLAUDE.md's bug-fix protocol; about 20 extra minutes.

options.label: Chore PR, no backlog ID
options.description: Fix plus one regression test, commit without an item ID. Fastest, but departs from the repo's 'every fix has an ID and trace' convention.

options.label: Fold into a later report-token-usage item
options.description: Don't open a PR now; note the two defects for whoever next touches the script (e.g. the chars/4 calibration finding from this analysis).

questions.question: Which interventions should the /ship variant for run B carry?

options.label: #1 Prose-tail stop
options.description: Once code and test findings stop, one final prose round, then file the rest. Targets the late rounds where 49–78% of findings repair earlier fixes.

options.label: #2 Fresh context at PR open
options.description: Fix rounds run from a fresh session or subagent fed the diff and findings, not the build context. Run A's compaction showed per-call cost falling about 9x on a reset.

options.label: #12 Orient: related open work
options.description: Before planning, list open items sharing the item's spec IDs or files and ask how they relate. Would have surfaced BK-389/BK-394 for BUG-280 at the start.

options.label: Gate robustness
options.description: One full suite at a time across sessions, a per-test timeout, a deadline on background waits. Removes the four cut-offs/hangs from run A's cost.

questions.question: Who builds the /ship variant?

options.label: token-usage2, after the RFC (Recommended)
options.description: The session that drafts the RFC builds the variant as its next PR. It holds the evidence and the design; it already runs in its own worktree.

options.label: A fresh session
options.description: A new session builds it from the merged RFC. Cleaner separation of author and builder; costs a re-orientation.

options.label: This session
options.description: I build it here. I know the data best, but this session's context is very large, so every call is expensive.

questions.question: Which code follow-ups should become backlog items now?

options.label: Gate robustness item
options.description: BUG or BK with the evidence: three hangs coincided with a second full suite; foreground gate median 195 s; four cut-offs in run A.

options.label: report_token_usage calibration
options.description: BK, small: 2.4 chars/token for tool results instead of 4, plus session prefix and hidden thinking in the ranking.

options.label: Escape-rate measurement
options.description: BK: count bugs found after merge in /ship PRs vs manual-era PRs; the one number that says whether /ship's extra cost buys quality.

options.label: Token kit pointer

options.label: Orient lesson
options.description: Check open items sharing spec IDs before planning an item; BUG-280 ran seven rounds before the BK-389/BK-394 link came up.

questions.question: The escape-rate measurement overlaps BK-366, whose dossier already plans an escaped/caught classification of every BUG-. File it as a new item, or fold it into BK-366?

options.label: New BK item
options.description: A separate BK-418 for the /ship escape-rate comparison, naming BK-366 as the related item. Two items then classify the same bugs.

options.label: Neither for now
options.description: Leave BK-366 untouched; the research record in token-usage2 carries the July finding and the escape-rate question.

options.description: Write a short trace per item recording the reads behind the filing (the analysis scripts and transcripts). More paperwork, and the traces would describe filing, not the work.
